A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIPGaussian framework and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-B. Retained material can be matched despite additions, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original stylization experiments across four modalities, quantitative comparisons, a 3D user study, and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, UVG experiments, consistency measurements, and failure-case analyses.

M1.justification: The Gaussian representations, four-term loss, patch augmentation, and modality-specific optimization procedures remain unchanged. CLIPGaussian-Light adjusts existing learning rates and patch-loss weights; it introduces no new architecture, loss component, or algorithmic step.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds four UVG sequences to the previously DAVIS-only video evaluation, extending coverage to longer videos under image and text conditioning. The four-modality task scope and other datasets, including the existing PanopticSports experiments, are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds SGSST and ABC-GS to the 3D image-conditioned comparison (Table 1), and ViSt3D, AdaAttN, and ReReVST to the DAVIS image-conditioned video comparison (Table 18). These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator sets. The user study retains its original methods.

E3.justification: v2 introduces flow-warped LPIPS/RMSE evaluation at frame offsets 1 and 7, and Farneback flow comparisons at offsets 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 (B.1.2). New protocols include Light configurations and 4D evaluation using 200 rendered views at 11 time points and 21 time points per test camera (B.3.4). The existing batch-size figure also relabels 3 as 4, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: The existing hyperparameter analyses are retained, while B.3.3 adds prompt-specificity and prompt-length experiments crossed with background-loss settings, examining semantic and background artifacts. v2 also adds standard-versus-Light comparisons and camera/time consistency analyses across batch sizes (B.3.4, Tables 16-17 and Figure 33).

E5.justification: The Friedman and Conover-Friedman tests, their p-value tables, and survey participant counts are retained. The added experiments do not introduce repeated-run or seed information, error bars, confidence intervals, or additional significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline and Light results, UVG scores, non-CLIP consistency measurements, and prompt/time findings. In the corresponding DAVIS image-conditioned comparison, CCPL's CLIP-S changes from 18.89 to 68.89 and UniST's from 15.93 to 65.93, while CLIPGaussian remains at 74.31 (v1 Table 14; v2 Table 18). These are revised reported values, without a documented explanation for the increases.

T1.justification: The representation and loss equations and existing CLIP metric definitions are unchanged. v2's added optical-flow formula documents an adopted evaluation metric; it introduces no new theoretical assumption, proof, derivation, or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of universal text/image-guided Gaussian stylization, joint appearance and geometry optimization, preserved model size, and strong quality and consistency. The additional experiments and Light configuration do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: B.3.3 substantially expands the failure discussion beyond v1's reconstruction dependence and 2D quality limitations. It relates prompt generality, specificity, and length to CLIP representation problems, unwanted semantic features, and background artifacts, explicitly explaining how higher CLIP scores can accompany worse perceived quality. Section 4 also adds a patch-size explanation for repeated structures in 2D outputs.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies Light settings: learning rate 0.002 and patch-loss weights 35 for 3D and 45 for video. v2 also specifies video resolutions and UVG downsampling, revises the reported 4D-scene hardware from RTX 4090 to DGX A100, and states that code is available rather than forthcoming after review. Most implementation documentation is retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of StyleDyRF, AdaAttN, ReReVST, ViSt3D, and StyleMaster, and elaborates the distinction from Instruct-GS2GS. Additional comparison and metric references include SGSST, ABC-GS, and StyleRF. This broadens the context while retaining the central novelty positioning; publication updates and consolidated duplicate references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: Localized editing streamlines the introduction and expands selected explanations. v2 adds appendix subsections, a social-impact paragraph, acknowledgments, and a NeurIPS checklist, and updates affiliations and conference information. The main section order and most retained prose remain stable.

P2.justification: The two original 3D comparison tables are merged and expanded into v2 Table 1; the DAVIS tables are similarly combined into Table 18. Numerous new analysis and consistency tables and Figures 19 and 31-33 substantially extend the displays. Existing figures are relocated, the survey screenshot is enlarged, and Figure 7 gains resolution; retained qualitative galleries largely preserve their content.

improvement.justification: v1's quantitative consistency evaluation relied on CLIP-derived measures. v2 substantially strengthens scrutiny of this central claim through non-CLIP consistency metrics, broader comparators, longer-video testing, and concrete prompt-failure analyses. These additions expose meaningful tradeoffs and applicability limits. The unchanged superiority wording remains overbroad: v2 Table 20 favors Rerender over standard CLIPGaussian on DAVIS LPIPS/RMSE. Despite that unresolved overstatement, the broader validation and explicit failure evidence provide a substantial net quality improvement.
